title: Second quantization and compactness of induced Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups
abstract: We characterize compactness of the Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful normal invariant state. A unitary second-quantization representation for every $ s $-embedding shows that compactness at one positive time, compact resolvent, drift stability, and uniqueness of the normal invariant state are equivalent. These conditions imply immediate trace-class membership for all embeddings. We derive exact trace-norm and Hilbert--Schmidt norm formulas, an embedding-independent trace identity, and the generator spectrum with algebraic multiplicities. Examples show that compactness does not require the existence of a spectral gap and that a spectral gap need not imply compactness when the invariant state is not unique.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups by characterizing the compactness of their induced semigroups. It proves that compactness is equivalent to several key stability conditions, such as having a compact resolvent and a unique invariant state. The methodology uses advanced second quantization techniques to derive explicit formulas for the spectrum and norms of the system's generator.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the compactness of Hilbert-Schmidt semigroups induced by finite-mode Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups and establishes equivalences between this compactness and other physical properties.
main_result: Compactness is equivalent to the compact resolvent, drift stability, and the uniqueness of the normal invariant state. Furthermore, the spectral properties of the generator are explicitly determined.
method: The study employs second quantization techniques to analyze the induced semigroups, relating the quantum dynamics to properties of the associated one-particle operators and their weighted covariance matrices.
model_or_system: The model concerns Gaussian quantum Markov semigroups (QMSs), which describe bosonic dynamics characterized by quadratic Hamiltonians and linear noise operators, acting on Fock spaces.
key_observables: The generator spectrum $\sigma(L(s))$, the spectral gap ($	ext{gap } L$), the resolvent operator $(L(s) - \lambda I)^{-1}$, and the induced semigroups $T^{(s)}_t$.
important_parameters: The embedding parameter $s \in [0, 1]$, which governs the relationship between different representations of the semigroup.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on the Gaussian assumption for the invariant state, although results are extended to general faithful normal invariant states.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the equivalence of several stability and compactness conditions (Chunk 1). It then details the mathematical machinery using second quantization to calculate weighted covariance matrices and identify the generator on the Hilbert-Schmidt space (Chunk 2). Finally, it performs a detailed spectral analysis of the generator, comparing spectral gaps and resolvent properties (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to analyze the long-time behavior and stability of open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding thermalization and dissipation in quantum many-body physics.
